correctness.rationale: For each nonzero translation, slicing the strictly convex body parallel to that translation gives strictly convex lower endpoints, strictly concave upper endpoints, and therefore a strictly concave chord-width function. Every positive width level lies in the boundary of a convex superlevel set and is null in the base; local Lipschitz regularity of the endpoint graph transfers this to zero surface measure on the boundary intersection. Ortega-Cerdà's full primary paper was inspected at Remark 6.4, and surface measure then satisfies each hypothesis of that boundary criterion.

originality.rationale: Ortega-Cerdà's primary theorem covers bounded convex open sets with C² boundary and separately states the more general boundary-measure criterion. Its proof uses a positively curved patch in the C² case; it does not state the nonsmooth strictly convex extension. Resultary and synonymous searches located no earlier theorem covering all bounded strictly convex bodies without boundary regularity.

value.rationale: Removing all boundary smoothness from a new nonexistence theorem on the natural class of strictly convex bodies is a substantive geometric extension, and the boundary-translate lemma isolates a reusable geometric mechanism.
